R741.note: Removes the ignoringRequestMatchers exclusion entirely, restoring default CSRF validation for /api/billing/**; matches stated contract.

R742.note: Moves the route to protectedMux; method check and profile route untouched, matches contract exactly.

R743.note: Allowlist of 4 report names closes the injection but is invented (no source confirms these are the complete valid set) and isn't flagged as needing verification; also the secondary hardening (System.setProperty at request time) is likely a no-op since such JDK ProcessImpl flags are typically cached at class-init, not re-read per call.

R744.note: Removes [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken]; app-wide AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute takes over cleanly.

R745.note: Switches to Winston meta-object logging; JSON.stringify of the meta escapes CR/LF, closing injection. Log line format change is disclosed.

R746.note: Binds '%'.term.'%' as a single parameter, preserving LIKE '%...%' semantics exactly as required by the contract.

R747.note: `from flask import escape` was removed in Flask 2.3 (2023) - flask.escape no longer exists, so this raises ImportError and crashes the whole app at import time, silently breaking the endpoint. Should import from markupsafe instead; the underlying idea (drop render_template_string, HTML-escape the name) is otherwise correct.

R748.note: Allowlist maps command words to fixed function names and calls them directly, eliminating any user-controlled dispatch; safe regardless of the exact original $$cmd mechanics (explanation mischaracterizes it as plain variable-function invocation, but the fix itself is sound).

R749.note: Replaces manual decode with firebase/php-jwt Key-bound HS256 verification; fails closed on bad signature.

R750.note: Array-form exec() closes shell metacharacter injection, the reported vector. Leading-dash flag injection into ping is a lesser residual risk the write-up only offers as optional hardening, not required for this finding.

R751.note: crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex') is a correct, drop-in replacement for the token source.

R752.note: SecureRandom + Base64 URL-safe string is a valid cookie/session value, preserves equality-based lookup usage.

R753.note: Encode.forHtml() applied to both author and comment at the concatenation point, closing both injection points.

R754.note: Splits GET (renders confirmation form) from a new CSRF-protected POST that performs the deletion; generateCsrfToken matches the current csrf-csrf API. Behavior change (one extra confirm click) is disclosed and doesn't block a legitimate user.

R755.note: Replaces PythonEngine.Execute with a fixed dispatch table (the KB's own recommended pattern for un-sandboxable eval), but the code as written is missing `using System.Linq;` for `.Reverse()`, so it won't compile as given. Also eliminates the actual custom-script feature the endpoint exists for; this trade-off is described in the write-up but not flagged as a required follow-up decision.

R756.note: Parameterized query matches the case's required behavior (exact-match search) precisely; correctly leaves search.js untouched.

R757.note: Rewrites the wire writer to build proper RESP arrays; SendSetCommand's signature is unchanged so no caller updates are needed.

R758.note: Changes subscribe() to take shared_ptr<Observer>, but the only caller in this case (sensor_monitor.cpp) passes a raw pointer to a stack-allocated SensorObserver and isn't updated - this breaks compilation of the call chain, and if force-adapted by wrapping the stack object in a shared_ptr it would double-free on scope exit.

R759.note: finfo-based content detection, allowlist, and randomized filename correctly close the extension-spoofing vector; execution-prevention assumption is stated openly.

R760.note: Moves the unique_ptr into the lambda's capture; matches the existing by-value signature exactly, no caller changes needed, satisfies the stated contract.

R761.note: HtmlEncode() at the concatenation point neutralizes markup while preserving the same Response.Write output shape.

R762.note: `Image.TryIdentifyFormat(stream, out format)` does not appear to be a real ImageSharp API (the library exposes DetectFormat/Identify, not a TryIdentifyFormat method), so this likely fails to compile as written; the overall approach (validate real image bytes, derive extension from detected format) is otherwise correct.

R763.note: JSON-encoding the label for the JS context is the right idea, but the fix drops @Html.Raw(): Razor's default @ output HTML-encodes the JsonSerializer.Serialize() result, turning the JSON string's quote characters into ", which breaks the <script> block's JS syntax on every render, not just malicious ones - this silent breakage isn't mentioned.

R764.note: RandomNumberGenerator.Fill + hex encoding is a correct, appropriately-sized replacement for Guid.NewGuid().

R765.note: SafeUnpickler class allowlist is the right primary technique, but it's gated behind a mandatory HMAC signature check the nightly batch-training producer (explicitly out of scope) doesn't emit, so every legitimate cache hit returns 500 until the producer is updated in lockstep - this coordination requirement is disclosed in the explanation, not hidden.

R766.note: Adds an explicit socket.user.role check inside the admin:broadcastMessage handler, matching the pattern already used by the other handler in the file.

R767.note: CBC with a random IV closes the ECB weakness; prepending the IV to the returned ciphertext is the necessary, disclosed way to make CBC decryptable, not an incidental side effect.

R768.note: Replaces raw inline-protocol socket writes with Apache Commons Net FTPClient, which frames commands itself; original code was already a non-functional stub (no server response handling or data-connection read), so no working behavior is lost.

R769.note: ObjectInputFilter allowlist matches the actual package (evalcases.OrderEvent); rejection surfaces through the existing catch(Exception) into RuntimeException, matching the contract exactly.

R770.note: Replaces node-serialize with JSON.parse + Joi schema validation; this is a single-file case with the server as the only visible cookie producer, so the format change is safe and is stated plainly.

R771.note: Regex-validates both addresses as well-formed emails before use, rejecting CRLF and other injection characters.

R772.note: jwt.decode() now passes the secret and pins algorithms=["HS256"], matching PyJWT 2.8.0's API and closing the verify_signature bypass.

R773.note: Parameterizes both tenantId and beforeDate; malformed dates still fail via SQL Server's type conversion rather than altering the predicate, satisfying the contract.

R774.note: ConstantTimeCompare only fixes the timing side-channel on a plaintext comparison; it leaves the actual root cause the case narrative flags ("the password column has always held the value the user typed at signup, unhashed") completely unaddressed - passwords are still stored and verified without hashing.

R775.note: strnlen(name, sizeof(name)) bounds the read to the field and cannot read into flags; matches the stated contract.

R776.note: `Map<String, ValidationRule> ruleRegistry = new EnumMap<>(ValidationRule.class)` is a type mismatch - EnumMap's key type is inferred as ValidationRule from the constructor argument, not String, so this won't compile as written. Also eliminates the tenant-authored custom-rule capability entirely, which the write-up frames as the intended design rather than a disclosed trade-off requiring sign-off.

R777.note: Encode.forHtml() plus print() (in place of format()) closes both the XSS and the format-string interpretation of the Referer header; matches the standard remediation for this benchmark pattern.

R778.note: json_encode() produces a valid escaped JS string literal for the script context, correctly closing the break-out vector.

R779.note: Registry-based indirection eliminates the traversal vector, but silently narrows what was a drop-in ./plugins/*.js directory (per the file's own comment) to two hardcoded names; the code comment flags where to add more, so this is visible rather than hidden, but the loss of extensibility isn't called out as a decision needing confirmation.

R780.note: secrets.choice() over the same alphabet and length preserves the 32-character token format exactly as the contract requires.
